preamble: No direct change of an aspirated stop [tʰ] to [s] is securely documented. The example formerly given here, the High German Consonant Shift (Proto-Germanic *watōr > Old High German wazzar, German Wasser; English water is a cognate, not the source), involves plain Proto-Germanic *t and is usually described as passing through an affricate or fortis fricative stage, so it belongs under t_to_ts and ts_to_s. Laconian Greek σ for Attic θ (σιός for θεός) is generally read as evidence that θ had already become a fricative [θ], which makes it a tʰ > θ > s chain as well.

examples.to: Old High German wazzar, German Wasser
examples.note: Postvocalic *t shifted to a sibilant fricative written zz; the input was plain *t and the change is analyzed via an affricate stage, so this is not a direct tʰ > s change.

sources: Campbell, L. (2013). Historical Linguistics: An Introduction (3rd ed.). Edinburgh University Press.
